arxiv-2106-13447.title: Spontaneous decay of artificial atoms in a three-qubit system
arxiv-2106-13447.creator: Ya. S. Greenberg, A. A. Shtygashev, A. G. Moiseev
arxiv-2106-13447.description: Abstract We study the evolution of qubits amplitudes in a one-dimensional chain consisting of three equidistantly spaced noninteracting qubits embedded in an open waveguide. The study is performed in the frame of single-excitation subspace, where the only qubit in the chain is initially excited.

arxiv-2304-12505.title: Theory of Posterior Concentration for Generalized Bayesian Additive Regression Trees
arxiv-2304-12505.creator: Enakshi Saha
arxiv-2304-12505.description: Abstract Bayesian Additive Regression Trees (BART) are a powerful semiparametric ensemble learning technique for modeling nonlinear regression functions. Although initially BART was proposed for predicting only continuous and binary response variables, over the years multiple extensions have emerged that are suitable for estimating a wider class of response variables (e.g. categorical and count data) in a multitude of application areas.

arxiv-2305-11426.title: Post Hoc Explanations of Language Models Can Improve Language Models
arxiv-2305-11426.creator: Satyapriya Krishna 1 , Jiaqi Ma 2 , Dylan Slack 3 , Asma Ghandeharioun 4 , Sameer Singh 3 , and Himabindu Lakkaraju 1 1 Harvard University 2 University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign 3 University of California, Irvine 4 Google Inc skrishna@g.harvard.edu
arxiv-2305-11426.description: Abstract Large Language Models (LLMs) have demonstrated remarkable capabilities in performing complex tasks. Moreover, recent research has shown that incorporating human-annotated rationales (e.g., Chain-of-Thought prompting) during in-context learning can significantly enhance the performance of these models, particularly on tasks that require reasoning capabilities.

arxiv-2306-09316.title: Diffusion Models for Open-Vocabulary Segmentation
arxiv-2306-09316.creator: Laurynas Karazija, Iro Laina, Andrea Vedaldi, Christian Rupprecht
arxiv-2306-09316.description: Abstract Open-vocabulary segmentation is the task of segmenting anything that can be named in an image. Recently, large-scale vision-language modelling has led to significant advances in open-vocabulary segmentation, but at the cost of gargantuan and increasing training and annotation efforts.

arxiv-2307-16551.title: High-speed data processing onboard sunrise chromospheric infrared spectropolarimeter for the Sunrise III balloon telescope
arxiv-2307-16551.creator: Masahito Kubo, Yukio Katsukawa, David Hernández Expósito, Antonio Sánchez Gómez, María Balaguer Jimenéz, David Orozco Suárez, José M. Morales Fernández, Beatriz Aparicio del Moral, Antonio J. Moreno Mantas, Eduardo Bailón Martínez, Jose Carlos del Toro Iniesta, Yusuke Kawabata, Carlos Quintero Noda,
arxiv-2307-16551.description: Abstract The Sunrise Chromospheric Infrared spectroPolarimeter (SCIP) has been developed for the third flight of the Sunrise balloon-borne stratospheric solar observatory. The aim of SCIP is to reveal the evolution of three-dimensional magnetic fields in the solar photosphere and chromosphere using spectropolarimetric measurements with a polarimetric precision of 0.03% (1 σ \sigma ).

arxiv-2407-19580.title: Mini-batch Coresets for Memory-efficient Language Model Training on Data Mixtures
arxiv-2407-19580.creator: Dang Nguyen, Wenhan Yang, Rathul Anand, Yu Yang, Baharan Mirzasoleiman
arxiv-2407-19580.description: Abstract Training with larger mini-batches improves the convergence rate and can yield superior performance. However, training with large mini-batches becomes prohibitive for Large Language Models (LLMs), due to the large GPU memory requirement. To address this problem, an effective approach is finding small mini-batch coresets that closely match the gradient of larger mini-batches.

arxiv-2409-17467.title: What is the social benefit of hate speech detection research? A Systematic Review
arxiv-2409-17467.creator: Sidney G.-J. Wong
arxiv-2409-17467.description: Abstract While NLP research into hate speech detection has grown exponentially in the last three decades, there has been minimal uptake or engagement from policy makers and non-profit organisations. We argue the absence of ethical frameworks have contributed to this rift between current practice and best practice.

arxiv-2508-09675.title: Time-Domain Reconstruction of the Speed of Sound in Ring-Array Ultrasound Computed Tomography with Randomized Super-Shots
arxiv-2508-09675.creator: Luca A. Forte
arxiv-2508-09675.description: Abstract Ring-array ultrasound computed tomography has recently achieved sufficient maturity for clinical applications like breast imaging. Image reconstruction is achieved with state of art iterative algorithms (full waveform inversion in the frequency domain). In this Letter, we consider a stochastic reconstruction in the time-domain.

arxiv-2509-09689.title: Personas within Parameters: Fine-Tuning Small Language Models with Low-Rank Adapters to Mimic User Behaviors
arxiv-2509-09689.creator: Himanshu Thakur, Eshani Agrawal, Smruthi Mukund
arxiv-2509-09689.description: Abstract A long-standing challenge in developing accurate recommendation models is simulating user behavior, mainly due to the complex and stochastic nature of user interactions. Towards this, one promising line of work has been the use of Large Language Models (LLMs) for simulating user behavior.

arxiv-2512-19019.title: Optimizer Dynamics at the Edge of Stability with Differential Privacy
arxiv-2512-19019.creator: Ayana Hussain, Ricky Fang
arxiv-2512-19019.description: Abstract Deep learning models can reveal sensitive information about individual training examples, and while differential privacy (DP) provides guarantees restricting such leakage, it also alters optimization dynamics in poorly understood ways. We study the training dynamics of neural networks under DP by comparing Gradient Descent (GD), and Adam to their privacy-preserving variants.

britannica-1911-cuthbert-saint.title: Cuthbert, Saint (1911 Encyclopaedia Britannica article)
britannica-1911-cuthbert-saint.creator: Encyclopaedia Britannica
britannica-1911-cuthbert-saint.description: Article 'Cuthbert, Saint' from the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica (Volume 7), the classic English-language general encyclopedia, now in the public domain. probably a Northumbrian by birth. According to the extant Lives he was led to take the monastic vows by a vision at the death of bishop Aidan, and the date of his entry at Melrose would be 651.

pmc-11480463.title: Efficient memristor accelerator for transformer self-attention functionality
pmc-11480463.creator: Meriem Bettayeb, Yasmin Halawani, Muhammad Umair Khan, Hani Saleh, Baker Mohammad
pmc-11480463.description: The adoption of transformer networks has experienced a notable surge in various AI applications. However, the increased computational complexity, stemming primarily from the self-attention mechanism, parallels the manner in which convolution operations constrain the capabilities and speed of convolutional neural networks (CNNs).

pmc-12522405.title: Trajectories of physical activity patterns across the life course in Mexican adults: findings from the Mexico city prospective study
pmc-12522405.creator: Eduardo Rossato de Victo, Leandro F M Rezende, Adilson Marques, Marcelo de Maio Nascimento, Diego Giulliano Destro Christofaro, Destro Christofaro, Gerson Ferrari
pmc-12522405.description: ObjectiveThe present study aimed to identify factors associated with distinct trajectories of physical activity (PA) patterns in Mexican adults during a 16-year follow-up.MethodsWe included 9,958 adults aged 35 years or older enrolled in The Mexico City Prospective Study, a prospective cohort study conducted from 1998 to 2004 to 2015–2019.

pmc-13018327.title: Management of type 2 diabetes mellitus using Yoga: Implications for immunological and autonomic dysfunction
pmc-13018327.creator: Rukadikar C.A, Geetha M, Dixit A.M, Renuka K, Vinoth R, Nishad S, Rukadikar A.R, Singh M.K
pmc-13018327.description: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is characterized by chronic hyperglycaemia, insulin resistance and β-cell dysfunction, leading to systemic inflammation and autonomic nervous system impairment. Diabetic autonomic neuropathy and cardiac autonomic neuropathy significantly increase risks of cardiovascular morbidity and mortality. Metabolic disturbances such as oxidative stress, polyol pathway activation and AGEs contribute to progressive neuronal and microvascular injury.

pmc-13026872.title: Hypoattenuation Pattern on Contrast-Enhanced Computed Tomography Predicts Poor Prognosis in Patients with Pancreatic Neuroendocrine Tumors
pmc-13026872.creator: Issei Kojima, Shinichi Hashimoto, Yu Yamazato, Ryusuke Shibata, Yusuke Kamikihara, Koshiro Toyodome, Takafumi Hamada, Makoto Hinokuchi, Shiho Arima, Shiroh Tanoue, Fumisato Sasaki, Fumitaka Ejima, Koji Takumi, Takashi Yoshiura, Shuji Kanmura
pmc-13026872.description: Background/Objectives: Several reports have shown that the hypoattenuation pattern of contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CECT) in pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors (PanNETs) is associated with poor overall survival (OS). However, these studies also included neuroendocrine carcinoma. Therefore, this study retrospectively investigated the relationship between attenuation patterns and OS, specifically in PanNETs.

pmc-13079861.title: Multicriteria site suitability for solar-powered green hydrogen production plants along the Northwestern coast of Egypt
pmc-13079861.creator: Abdel-hameed M. El-Aassar, Kamilia H. Hagagg, Rasha A. Hussien
pmc-13079861.description: An integrated geospatial, hydrogeochemical framework for identifying environmentally suitable locations for solar-powered green hydrogen production along Egypt’s northwestern Mediterranean coast is applied. The methodology combines environmental stable isotope of groundwater (δ1⁸O and δ2H) for quaternary, upper miocene, and lower miocene aquifers with multi-criteria spatial analysis in geographic information system (GIS).

pmc-13081783.title: Exploring the relationship between migraine and mental health – perspectives from the patient and physician experience
pmc-13081783.creator: Jaclyn E. Klepper, Heather Moran, Lawrence Newman
pmc-13081783.description: ObjectiveThere is growing interest in the impact of multimorbidity in migraine, especially between migraine and mental health conditions. The relationship between migraine and mental health is bi-directional, people with migraine are more likely to experience anxiety and depression and people with anxiety and depression are more likely to experience migraine.

pmc-13259159.title: Integrating Eye Tracking in Acoustic Research: Methods for Sound Localization, Event Detection, Multimodal Sensing, and Perceptual Analysis
pmc-13259159.creator: Giuseppe Ciaburro, Virginia Puyana-Romero
pmc-13259159.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Recent advances in eye-tracking technologies have fostered growing interest in their integration with acoustic research for investigating auditory perception and human behavioral responses. This study presents a structured literature review of recent developments at the intersection of eye tracking and acoustics, with the aim of analyzing how eye-movement data can support the interpretation of auditory events, spatial listening behaviors, and multimodal human–environment interactions.
